title: Will and Portrait
premise: Edmund Thornbury, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made him the unofficial archivist of the town of Marrow's Bend, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove that a murder will not happen — a murder dated three days in the future, in a house everyone believes burned down twelve years ago. As Edmund investigates, he realizes the predicted killing mirrors one from his own past: the fire that killed the Calloway family, a case he closed himself and has never been able to stop re-reading in his mind. The client is the 'victim' — a woman officially dead since that fire — and Edmund must decide whether exposing the truth about what really happened twelve years ago is worth destroying the town's fragile peace and his own carefully filed life. In the end, Edmund catches the would-be killer, the town's beloved doctor who started the original fire to cover a malpractice death, but chooses to publish only part of the truth, learning that some memories are carried rather than solved.
about_author: Yara Oyelaran is a former claims adjuster turned novelist who grew up in a small river town where everyone kept two sets of records. She writes mysteries about people who remember too much and forgive too little.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A pale, unremarkable client named Vera Lune walks into Thornbury Investigations and pays to prevent a murder scheduled for Friday night at Holloway House — a ruin that burned in 2012. Edmund's memory instantly flags her face as familiar. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional calm; the hook of an impossible commission.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. He pulls his mental files on Holloway House and the Calloway fire, walking the reader through the town's sealed narrative: accidental blaze, four dead, case closed by young investigator Edmund himself. His assistant Dara notices him rattled for the first time in years. Emotional beat: the first crack in twelve years of tidy filing.

chapters.title: A Woman with No Records
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Digging into Vera Lune, Edmund finds she doesn't exist — no birth record, no tax history — yet her fingerprints match a girl listed dead in the fire: Ivy Calloway, seventeen. He confronts her; she admits nothing except that someone means to kill her again. Emotional beat: vertigo of a past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Doctor Ordered
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. He interviews Dr. Ambrose Pell, town patriarch and the fire's investigating physician, whose charm sets off every alarm Edmund owns. Meanwhile anonymous warnings appear on Edmund's door: CLOSE THE FILE. Emotional beat: rising dread as the town's benevolent face shows its seams.

chapters.title: Dara Asks Too Many Questions
chapters.summary: POV Dara. Shifting perspective, Dara secretly audits Edmund's old case file and finds pages altered — dates shifted, a fifth name redacted. She realizes her meticulous boss may have made the town's biggest mistake, or been made to. Emotional beat: loyalty tested; the apprentice sees the master's flaw.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund and Vera break into the rebuilt shell of Holloway House, where Vera relives the night of the fire: she saw Pell inject her dying father to silence a malpractice witness, then flee as flames spread. Edmund's photographic recall reconstructs the scene against his own written report — they don't match. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Pell confronts Edmund privately, offering the gentle blackmail of complicity: Edmund signed the closure; unsealing it ends his career and maybe Dara's safety. Edmund spends a sleepless night cataloguing everything survival has cost him. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes — the price of staying safe is never being honest.

chapters.title: Friday
chapters.summary: POV alternating Edmund/Dara. The predicted night arrives. Dara traces the 'murder' tip to a second party watching Vera; Edmund stakes out Holloway House as Pell arrives to finish what the fire started. A chase through the gutted rooms; Dara arrives with police just as Pell corners them. Emotional beat: climax — terror sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Confession in Ash
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Trapped and exposed, Pell confesses — not to Edmund, but to Vera, believing her testimony worthless against his standing. But Edmund has been recording, and more damningly, reciting Pell's own words back verbatim, memory as weapon. Arrest follows. Emotional beat: catharsis; the archive finally testifies.

chapters.title: Belonging, Amended
chapters.summary: POV Vera, closing on Edmund. Vera chooses to leave Marrow's Bend alive rather than reclaim a stolen childhood, while Edmund publishes the corrected report but omits the town's smaller shames — a mercy he once would have called corruption. He keeps one page for himself. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; memory kept, not erased; belonging redefined.
